g.text: domain adlab.test 33 accounts 41 cert templates 2026-11-05 01:57 UTC
ESC8: web enrollment accepts NTLM over HTTP
Coerced NTLM authentication from a DC can be relayed to these endpoints to obtain a
certificate for the DC and then DCSync.
Disable HTTP on the web enrollment site, require HTTPS with Extended Protection for
Authentication, or remove web enrollment if it is unused.
LDAP signing not required and LDAPS channel binding not enforced, and any user can create
computer accounts: coerced authentication from a server can be relayed to LDAP to set up
resource-based delegation and log on to that server as an admin.
Require LDAP signing and channel binding, and set ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota to 0.
Credentials in SYSVOL or NETLOGON scripts
Every domain user can read SYSVOL and NETLOGON; these lines appear to contain a literal
password (the value is not reproduced here).
Remove the credentials from the scripts and change the passwords.
BadSuccessor: dMSA creation rights outside tier 0
On Windows Server 2025 domains, anyone who can create a dMSA in a container can make it
inherit the rights of any account, including domain admins.
AdminSDHolder: helpdesk, Lab: ou_admin, adlab: helpdesk
Remove CreateChild/GenericAll/WriteDacl/WriteOwner for these principals and install
Control paths from non-tier-0 principals to tier 0
5 principals outside tier 0 can reach it; 18 of 19 enabled users (94%) have a path through
their accounts or groups. Each object shows the shortest path. Broad groups have a path, so
Domain Users -[enroll (ESC1-3)]-> template LabESC1, gpo_linker -[link GPOs]->
Break each path at its first step, starting with the ones shared by most paths (see
note: no fine-grained password policy visible (none exist, or this account cannot read them); AD-POL-001
judges the default domain policy only
